interest: This document illustrates the unique international reputation and demand for Japanese chick sexers in the post-World War II poultry industry, alongside the stringent travel restrictions imposed on Japanese nationals during the Allied Occupation. It offers insight into the diplomatic and commercial dynamics of post-war reconstruction, showing how foreign requests for specialized Japanese technical labor were evaluated against occupation travel directives and the competing presence of the American Chick Sexing Association.
overview: This file consists of a single confidential incoming telegram dated March 27, 1948, sent from Tokyo to the Department of State regarding a request by the Belgian Government to employ Japanese chick sexers. The telegram states that the proposed travel of Japanese nationals for this purpose does not fall under permitted travel categories specified in directive W-95467 and is therefore not favorably considered. It also notes that chick sexing services were already accessible in Belgium through the American Chick Sexing Association.

subfiles.about: Reports the rejection of a Belgian request to employ Japanese chick sexers due to travel restrictions under Allied Occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: An incoming confidential telegram from Tokyo to the Department of State addressing the Belgian Government's request to use Japanese chick sexers. It reports that after careful consideration, the travel is not considered to fall within the authorized categories for Japanese nationals established under directive W-95467 and is thus not favorably considered. It adds that chick sexing services are available in Belgium via the American Chick Sexing Association.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Tokyo to Department of State on proposed use of Japanese chick sexers in Belgium
